say.en: When you send a WhatsApp message, there is you, your friend, the message, the mobile network, and a set of rules both phones follow. Remove any one and the message does not arrive. In this lesson: List the five components of data communication.
Define bandwidth and data transfer rate.
Calculate transfer time.

body.en: *Data communication* is the exchange of data between two or more networked devices. It has five components: the sender (sends the message), the receiver (receives it), the message (text, audio, video, image, numbers), the communication medium (the path: wired or wireless), and protocols (the agreed rules for communication).

narration.en: Every data communication has a sender, a receiver, a message, a medium and protocols, which are the rules both sides follow.

title.en: On the board: Five components and the time to send a file

say.en: A sender sends a message to a receiver through a communication medium.
Both sides must follow the same protocol: the agreed rules for the format and the order of messages.
Bandwidth is the range of frequencies a channel carries: the highest minus the lowest frequency.
Data transfer rate is the number of bits sent each second. A byte is 8 bits, so a 100 MB file needs 800 megabits.
At 8 megabits per second it takes 800 divided by 8, that is 100 seconds.
Units go up in steps: Kbps, Mbps, Gbps, Tbps.

body.en: Bandwidth is the range of frequencies a channel can carry: the difference between the highest and lowest frequencies, measured in hertz (Hz). Higher bandwidth means more data can be carried. *Data transfer rate* (bit rate) is the number of bits sent per second, measured in bps, Kbps, Mbps, Gbps and Tbps; the textbook takes 1 Kbps = $2^{10}$ bps. Remember 1 byte = 8 bits.

myth.en: A 25 MB file on an 8 Mbps connection takes 25 / 8 ≈ 3 seconds.

truth.en: MB is megabytes and Mbps is megabits per second. Convert first: 25 MB = 200 Mb, so it takes 200 / 8 = 25 s. The letters look almost the same. File sizes are counted in bytes (B) but links are rated in bits (b), and one byte is 8 bits.

title.en: Types of data communication and switching

say.en: In a network, data from a sender usually passes through many switches before reaching the receiver. Switching decides how it travels.

goal.en: The five components of data communication, bandwidth and data transfer rate with numericals, simplex, half-duplex and full-duplex communication, and circuit versus packet switching.

explain.en: Simplex is one way, half-duplex is two ways taking turns, and full-duplex is two ways at the same time.

narration.en: Many people think: A 25 MB file on an 8 Mbps connection takes 25 / 8 ≈ 3 seconds. Actually: MB is megabytes and Mbps is megabits per second. Convert first: 25 MB = 200 Mb, so it takes 200 / 8 = 25 s. The letters look almost the same. File sizes are counted in bytes (B) but links are rated in bits (b), and one byte is 8 bits.

problem.en: A 50 MB video is sent over a 20 Mbps connection. How long does it take, ignoring overheads?

steps.en: Convert bytes to bits: 50 MB × 8 = 400 Mb.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. A 50 MB video is sent over a 20 Mbps connection. How long does it take, ignoring overheads?

say.en: Let us work through this together. A 50 MB video is sent over a 20 Mbps connection. How long does it take, ignoring overheads?
Convert bytes to bits: 50 MB times 8 equals 400 Mb.
Time equals data divided by rate equals 400 Mb divided by 20 Mbps.
Time equals 20 seconds.
So the answer is 20 seconds.

problem.en: An FM channel uses frequencies from 98.2 MHz to 98.4 MHz. Find its bandwidth.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. An FM channel uses frequencies from 98.2 MHz to 98.4 MHz. Find its bandwidth.

say.en: Let us work through this together. An FM channel uses frequencies from 98.2 megahertz to 98.4 megahertz. Find its bandwidth.
Bandwidth equals highest frequency - lowest frequency.
= 98.4 megahertz minus 98.2 megahertz equals 0.2 megahertz.
= 200 kilohertz.
So the answer is 0.2 megahertz equals 200 kilohertz.
